old_caption: The video captures a blacksmith at work in a workshop setting. The blacksmith, dressed in a light-colored shirt and wearing yellow gloves for protection, is focused on shaping a glowing red-hot piece of metal. The metal is held securely in a vise attached to a large, industrial-looking hammer press. The hammer press, with its metallic body and robust design, dominates the scene, poised above the glowing metal. The blacksmith uses tongs to maneuver the hot metal, carefully positioning it under the press head. The background features a dark brick wall, adding to the rustic and industrial atmosphere of the workshop. A large cylindrical object, possibly a drum or container, is visible to the left, suggesting additional tools or materials might be stored there. The lighting is dim, emphasizing the bright glow of the heated metal and creating a dramatic contrast with the surrounding shadows. The blacksmith's hands are actively adjusting the tongs, maintaining control over the hot metal as it is positioned for the next strike.

caption: The video captures a blacksmithing scene in a dim workshop backed by a dark brick wall, with a metal drum at the left and a vertical power hammer at the center. A man in a grey shirt and a yellow protective glove leans over the machine, gripping a glowing orange-hot billet with long tongs on the anvil die. The cylindrical ram of the hammer hangs above the workpiece, which stays incandescent throughout. Two spare tongs and metal rods lie on the worktable in the foreground. As the sequence runs, the ram descends toward the billet and lifts again in repeated cycles, consistent with the machine striking the hot metal. Between these movements the smith's gloved hand shifts the tongs, repositioning and turning the billet on the die. His head and torso adjust subtly as he watches and feeds the work under the tool. The background elements remain fixed, indicating an essentially static camera. The forging process is already underway at the first frame and continues past the last, with the billet still bright and the hammer still cycling.

If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
